title: Which of three distances in space is the smallest?
description: The book gives the distances from the Sun to Saturn, from Saturn to Uranus and from the Sun to the Earth, each in scientific form. The powers of ten are compared first, and then the Earth is placed on a line from the Sun to Saturn. Keeko doubts that the biggest number in front makes the biggest distance.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare numbers in scientific form, compare the powers of ten first, then the numbers in front. Watch for students who pick the number with the biggest digits in front.

source: Which is the smallest of the distances Sun to Saturn (1.4335
video_script.why: Numbers in scientific form are compared by the power of ten first. When two powers match, the numbers in front decide.
video_script.substitution: Compare the powers of ten; then write two numbers with the same power to place one on a line against the other.
video_script.anchor: three distances in space and a line from the Sun to Saturn
video_script.wrong_answer: Sun to Earth is the largest
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko compares only the numbers in front, sees that 1.496 is the biggest, and calls the Sun to Earth distance the largest. The power of ten is smaller there, so the number is smaller.
video_script.payoff_line: Compare the powers of ten first, and then the numbers in front

final_answer.value: Sun to Earth is the smallest; the Earth is about one tenth of the way from the Sun to Saturn
final_answer.spoken: The distance from the Sun to the Earth is the smallest. The Earth is about one tenth of the way from the Sun to Saturn.

video_script.fraction_reading: one tenth of the way along the line
hold_back: Sun to Earth is the smallest
maths_rules: the slip: 1.496 is the biggest number in front, but the power is 11 against 12
video_script.design: A line from the Sun to Saturn is drawn in the last step and the Earth is placed on it. The three distances sit in a short table in the working area.

beats.on_screen: a small title card, From your book; three distances appear one by one: Sun to Saturn 1.4335 × 10¹² m, Saturn to Uranus 1.439 × 10¹² m, Sun to Earth 1.496 × 10¹¹ m

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='sat'/>The Sun to Saturn is one point four three three five times ten to the power twelve metres.
<bookmark mark='ura'/>Saturn to Uranus is one point four three nine times ten to the power twelve metres.
<bookmark mark='earth'/>The Sun to the Earth is one point four nine six times ten to the power eleven metres.
Which of these three distances is the smallest?

beats.on_screen: the three distances stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 10¹² = 10 × 10¹¹, shown as a bar of ten blocks next to one block

marks.first: the bar of ten blocks glows next to the single block

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten to the power twelve is ten times ten to the power eleven.
<bookmark mark='first'/>One step higher in the power makes a number ten times bigger.
The power of ten tells us the size before the digits do.

beats.on_screen: Given: Sun to Saturn 1.4335 × 10¹² m; Saturn to Uranus 1.439 × 10¹² m; Sun to Earth 1.496 × 10¹¹ m

marks.given: the three distances are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three distances in space, all in metres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the smallest distance; the place of the Earth on the line from the Sun to Saturn

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the smallest distance.
Then we place the Earth on a line from the Sun to Saturn.

marks.s1: the powers 12, 12 and 11 are circled in the column

beats.colours: the lowest power in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, look at the powers of ten.
Two distances have the power twelve, and one has the power eleven.

beats.on_screen: the lowest power gives the smallest distance

marks.s2: the circle around the power 11 glows

beats.colours: the lowest power in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, the lowest power gives the smallest distance.
The numbers in front do not change that.

marks.s3: the power 12 changes to 11 and the point moves one place right
marks.same: both distances now show the power 11

beats.moves_through: the point hops right by one place
narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, write the Sun to Saturn distance with the power eleven.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The power comes down by one, so the point moves one place to the right.
It becomes fourteen point three three five times ten to the power eleven.

beats.on_screen: 1.496 ÷ 14.335 ≈ 0.104; the line from the Sun to Saturn with the Earth marked

marks.line: the Earth is marked on the line from the Sun to Saturn at 0.104 of its length

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, divide one point four nine six by fourteen point three three five.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The result is close to zero point one, so the Earth sits near the start of the line.

beats.on_screen: Sun to Earth is the smallest; the Earth is about one tenth of the way from the Sun to Saturn

marks.pay: the words powers first, then the numbers in front appear
marks.ans1: Sun to Earth is the smallest is boxed
marks.ans2: the Earth is about one tenth of the way along the line is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Compare the powers of ten first, and then the numbers in front.
<bookmark mark='ans1'/>The distance from the Sun to the Earth is the smallest.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The Earth is about one tenth of the way from the Sun to Saturn.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand next to the answer lines
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble shows Sun to Earth is the largest, 1.496 is the biggest; 10¹¹ = 10¹² ÷ 10 is written; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour
beats.colours: the wrong bubble in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Sun to Earth is the largest.
Its number in front, one point four nine six, is the biggest of the three.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>But ten to the power eleven is one tenth of ten to the power twelve.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The power of ten matters far more than the number in front, so that thought is wrong.
